h-upmann-cuba--linea-clasica.description: The core H. Upmann range goes back to Herman Upmann, a German banker who opened a bank and a cigar factory in Havana in 1844; the medals on the box recall awards from eleven nineteenth-century fairs. Rolled entirely by hand with long filler from Vuelta Abajo leaf, it smokes light to medium, with cocoa, coffee and a soft leather note over a creamy draw.

thirds.notes: Rich cocoa over a salty, peppery opening, with sweet leather and a creamy edge as the early spice settles.
Semi-sweet chocolate and coffee take the lead, with wood and faint leather, vanilla and citrus in the background.
Coffee turns creamy and smooth, joined by light earth and cedar as the finish lengthens.

h-upmann-cuba--linea-magnum.description: H. Upmann's Magnum line has a presentation of its own: the Magnum 46 and Magnum 50, the latter presented in 2008, were joined by the Magnum 54 in 2016. Made by hand from Vuelta Abajo leaf, its blends are elegant and gentle, light to medium in strength. Nutty and lightly spiced at the start, it gathers pepper, coffee and cacao as it burns.

thirds.notes: Smooth and balanced, with peanut, a touch of anise and a dry, clay-like earthiness.
Cashew and nutmeg arrive with black pepper; the smoke thickens and turns markedly spicy.
Coffee grounds and cacao nibs close the smoke, with a sharp, mustard-like spice as the body builds.

sources.title: Bespoke Unit – H. Upmann Magnum 54 review

h-upmann-cuba--connoisseur.description: Within the Connossieur line, H. Upmann released the Connoisseur A in 2013 and the 54-ring Connoisseur B in 2017 for La Casa del Habano and Habanos Specialist shops. In 2020 the Connossieur No. 2, light in strength, joined the standard range as the first 51-ring cigar in the Habanos portfolio. Cedar, toast and nutmeg lead, turning towards citrus, earth and coffee.

thirds.notes: Cedar forms the base, with light pepper and nutmeg on a creamy, slightly oily smoke and a hint of toast.
Almond and toast join the cedar; the spice recedes and an orange-like citrus comes to the front.
Earth, grass and oak gather around the cedar, with a richer coffee and natural tobacco sweetness.

h-upmann-cuba--reserva-en-gran-reserva.description: H. Upmann's harvest-dated releases. The Upmann No. 2 Reserva Cosecha 2010, presented in 2014 as the brand's first Reserva, used 2010 leaf rested for three years and came in 5,000 numbered lacquered cases of 20. The Sir Winston Gran Reserva Cosecha 2011, a Churchill, followed in 2017 as the first Gran Reserva; it smokes silky and earthy, with coffee and bitter cocoa.

thirds.notes: A delicate, silky start with an earthy mushroom note and coffee softened by cream.
The smoke opens and grows more harmonious, with bitter cocoa over earthy, mineral undertones.
Flavours saturate into minerals and black pepper as the smoke turns heavier and more robust.

sources.title: Cigars Connect – H. Upmann Sir Winston Gran Reserva Cosecha 2011 review

h-upmann-cuba--edicion-limitada.description: H. Upmann's share of the annual Habanos Ediciones Limitadas: sizes outside the regular range, rolled from leaf aged at least two years under a darker wrapper cut from the top of the shade-grown plant, with a black and gold seal and an extra band naming the year. Releases include the Robustos of 2012, the 56-ring Magnum 56 of 2015 and the Propios of 2018.

sources.title: Habanos – Edición Limitada 2012 H. Upmann Robustos
Habanos – Ediciones Limitadas 2015: H. Upmann Magnum 56

h-upmann-cuba--coleccion-habanos-en-spec.description: Special H. Upmann productions outside the regular range. The Colección Habanos edition, sold through La Casa del Habano in a book-like cabinet, holds 20 Super Magnums of 56 x 180 mm, made in a run of 3,000 and marked by a second band at the foot. The 2019 jar of 20 Magnum 56 was made for duty-free and travel retail.
